references.text: The parable immediately before this, where Jesus tells of the two debtors—the one who was forgiven more loved more. This is the direct context for verse 47, which summarizes the point of the parable.
Jesus says directly to the woman that her sins are forgiven, confirming the statement in verse 47 that her many sins have been forgiven. Those at the table ask who this is who even forgives sins.
Jesus tells the woman that her faith has saved her, linking forgiveness of sins to faith. This complements verse 47 by showing that love is a sign of the forgiveness already received through faith.

Jesus says that the woman who anointed him with costly ointment will be remembered wherever the gospel is preached. This parallels the woman's act of love in Luke 7 as an expression of gratitude and love.
Paul writes that Christ's love was overwhelmingly great, accompanied by faith and love. Those who have experienced great grace show great love—parallel to the principle in Luke 7:47.
'We love because he first loved us.' This reflects the theological principle in Luke 7:47—love for God is a response to his prior forgiveness and grace.

Paul urges believers to forgive one another as Christ has forgiven them, and to clothe themselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect unity. Forgiveness and love are closely linked, as in Luke 7:47.
Paul encourages mutual forgiveness just as God in Christ has forgiven us. Those who have received forgiveness should show love and forgiveness—parallel to Jesus' point in Luke 7:47.
David praises the one whose sins are forgiven and whose transgressions are covered. This expresses the same joy and gratitude over forgiveness that the woman in Luke 7 demonstrated.
The Lord offers forgiveness: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. The great forgiveness God offers provides the basis for the great love described in Luke 7:47.

In the parable of the unforgiving servant, Jesus shows that those who have been forgiven much should show mercy. The principle is the same as in Luke 7:47: great forgiveness should lead to great love and mercy.
God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. Those who have experienced God's grace and forgiveness respond with love—in line with the principle of Luke 7:47.
